title: Interior Paint Color Live Previewer
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js that implements an interactive interior room paint color live previewer. The scene must be fully self-contained with no external dependencies except Three.js via CDN.

## Scene Setup
- Create a 3D room interior (box geometry viewed from inside): floor (8x8 units), ceiling at height 3.5, four walls.
- The room has: left wall, right wall, back wall, front wall (with a rectangular doorway cutout of width 1.5 and height 2.5 centered horizontally at floor level).
- Place a PointLight (warm white #FFF5E0, intensity 1.2) at center ceiling. Add AmbientLight (intensity 0.3).
- Camera starts at position (0, 1.6, 2.5) looking toward the back wall. OrbitControls with vertical angle clamped so user cannot look outside the room (min polar 0.3, max polar 2.2, min distance 1, max distance 5).
- Floor uses a subtle checkerboard pattern (two shades of gray). Ceiling is always white (#FFFFFF).

## Paintable Surfaces
- Each of the 4 walls is an independently paintable surface. They start with a default color of #E8E0D4 (warm beige).
- Walls must use MeshStandardMaterial with roughness 0.7 and metalness 0.0.

## UI / HUD Elements
- A DOM overlay panel on the left side (width 240px, semi-transparent dark background) containing:
  1. A title "Paint Previewer"
  2. A color palette with 8 preset color swatches displayed as clickable 36x36px divs in a 2x4 grid: #E8E0D4 (Warm Beige), #4A6741 (Forest Green), #2C3E6B (Navy Blue), #8B2500 (Burnt Sienna), #F5F0EB (Ivory), #6B4C6E (Plum), #C4A35A (Gold Ochre), #3A3A3A (Charcoal).
  3. A custom color input (HTML color picker input element, id='customColor').
  4. A "Finish" dropdown (id='finishSelect') with options: Matte (roughness 0.9), Eggshell (roughness 0.7), Satin (roughness 0.45), Semi-Gloss (roughness 0.25), Gloss (roughness 0.1).
  5. An "Apply to All Walls" button (id='applyAllBtn').
  6. An "Undo" button (id='undoBtn') and a "Redo" button (id='redoBtn').
  7. A text display (id='selectedWallLabel') showing which wall is currently selected (e.g., "Selected: Back Wall") or "No wall selected".
  8. A text display (id='currentColorLabel') showing the hex color of the currently selected wall.

## Interaction Mechanics
- WALL SELECTION: Raycasting on click. When user clicks on a wall in the 3D viewport, that wall becomes "selected". A subtle highlight outline or emissive glow (emissive color #333333) is applied to the selected wall. Only one wall can be selected at a time. Clicking empty space or floor/ceiling deselects.
- COLOR APPLICATION: When a wall is selected and user clicks a color swatch, the selected wall's material color changes to that swatch color. The custom color picker also applies its color on 'input' event if a wall is selected.
- FINISH APPLICATION: Changing the finish dropdown updates the roughness of the selected wall's material immediately.
- APPLY ALL: The 'Apply to All Walls' button applies the current selected color AND current finish to all 4 walls simultaneously.
- UNDO/REDO: Maintain a history stack of wall state changes. Each change records {wallId, previousColor, previousRoughness, newColor, newRoughness}. Undo reverts the last change. Redo re-applies. Max history depth of 50. Redo stack clears when a new action is performed.
- KEYBOARD: Press keys 1-4 to select walls (1=left, 2=right, 3=back, 4=front). Press 'U' for undo, 'R' for redo (only when not focused on an input element). Press 'Escape' to deselect all walls.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- walls: array of 4 objects [{id: 'left', color: '#RRGGBB', roughness: number, metalness: number}, ...] in order [left, right, back, front]
- selectedWall: string|null (the id of the selected wall or null)
- historyIndex: number (current position in history, starts at -1 meaning no actions yet)
- historyLength: number (total entries in history stack)
- undoCount: number (total undo operations performed)
- redoCount: number (total redo operations performed)
- currentFinish: string ('Matte'|'Eggshell'|'Satin'|'Semi-Gloss'|'Gloss')
- lightIntensity: number (point light intensity)
- cameraPosition: {x, y, z}
- applyAllCount: number (how many times Apply All was used)

Update window.__3D_STATE__ every frame in the animation loop to keep it in sync with the actual Three.js scene state. Read colors directly from the material's color property converted to hex string.
physics_constraints: Material roughness must be clamped [0.0, 1.0]. Metalness must remain 0.0 for all walls at all times. Colors must be valid 6-digit hex strings. Undo/redo must perfectly restore previous states (color AND roughness). History stack must not exceed 50 entries. Camera must remain inside room bounds.
